title: Build initial structures
action: Construct molecular models for the four variants of [Fe(L₁)Cl₃]: 1a (tetrahedral, Fe coordinated to N7 of L₁ and three Cl⁻, spin state S=5/2); 1b (N6 monodentate coordination with a proton shifted to N3); 1c (bidentate coordination via N6 and N7 with proton at N1); 1d (trigonal-bipyramidal, Fe coordinated to N7, three Cl⁻, and one water molecule, spin state S=3/2). Use the ligand's chemical structure (2-chloro-6-benzylamino-9-isopropylpurine) and the descriptions provided.
description: This step prepares the initial guesses for DFT optimization. No output file is submitted; the structures are passed internally to the next step.

title: DFT geometry optimization and frequency check
action: Optimize the geometry of each structure (1a-1d) using density functional theory at the B3LYP/6-311G(d)+Wachter's level. Perform harmonic vibrational frequency calculations to verify that the optimized structures are minima. Save the final optimized coordinates of all four structures in a single XYZ file.
description: Optimized geometries of 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d. The file should contain four molecules separated by standard XYZ format with comment lines indicating the model name and spin state. This artifact is scored via a structural audit (bond lengths, coordination numbers).
output_schema: XYZ file with multiple structures. Each molecule begins with the number of atoms on a line, followed by a comment line specifying '1a (S=5/2)', '1b', '1c', '1d (S=3/2)' etc., then lines with element symbol and x,y,z coordinates in Angstrom.

title: Mössbauer isomer shift calculation
action: From the optimized wavefunction/electron density of each structure, compute the non-relativistic electron density at the ⁵⁷Fe nucleus, ρ₀^A(0). Calculate the Mössbauer isomer shift δ (mm/s) using δ = α [ρ₀^A(0) - ρ₀^S(0)], where α = -0.395 mm s⁻¹ au³ and ρ₀^S = 11614.10 au⁻³. Report the shifts at 0 K (no Doppler correction). Output a JSON file with the computed shifts.
description: Computed ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer isomer shifts (0 K) for structures 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d. The checker will compare these values to the paper's theoretical values (hidden gold) with an exact-match tolerance of ±0.03 mm/s.
output_schema: JSON object with keys '1a', '1b', '1c', '1d' (all strings) and values being floats representing the isomer shift δ in mm/s (unitless in JSON).
